title: SDK lightweight inception playbook (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, intentionally opinionated playbook for the first 48 hours of a new SDK adopter or internal engineer starting an SDK integration. Focus: minimal friction, measurable wins, and a tiny set of experiments that validate the integration path without building a full app.

Audience:
- New SDK adopters (engineers at customer orgs)
- Internal solutions engineers running quick POCs
- Developer advocates running workshops

Scope and constraints:
- Narrow: server-to-server SDK usage (polyglot examples), local dev loop, core telemetry expectations.
- Excludes: enterprise on-prem packaging, advanced instrumentation, and deep security hardening (link out to compliance checklist).

Outcome (what success looks like in 48h):
- Hello-world flow up and authenticated in ~15 minutes.
- One deterministic prompt/feature validated against real traffic shape (latency + cost sanity).
- Minimal telemetry: request count, 95p latency, token cost per request.
- A short experiment note saved in the repo (README + 1 screenshot or trace).

First-48h checklist (practical steps) — prioritized:
1) Pre-flight (0–15m)
   - Create API key / confirm org access.
   - Clone example repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/examples (pick language).
   - Run local sample off-host mode if you have constraints.

2) Hello-path (15–45m)
   - Run the minimal sample that sends a 1-turn prompt and streams output to terminal.
   - Confirm streaming vs non-streaming behavior and token-count returned by SDK.
   - Note: if streaming is slow, capture trace id and attach to support ticket.

3) Instrument a single metric (45–90m)
   - Add simple client-side wrapper that logs: request id, model name, prompt length (tokens), duration_ms.
   - Push one example event to your telemetry (console is fine for the experiment).

4) Micro-experiment: latency vs batching (90–180m)
   - Run 10 sequential single-request runs and record median & 95p.
   - Run a batched run (if client supports) and compare cost per output token + latency.
   - Document results in experiment/very-small-notes.md.

5) Sanity prompt fidelity check (2–6h)
   - Pick 10 representative prompts, run twice with pinned model version, compare outputs.
   - If >20% drift in quality, flag as 'model mismatch' and capture top 3 examples.

15-minute quickstart (concise commands)
- Linux/macOS minimal flow (bash):
  # clone
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk/examples.git && cd examples/java-minimal
  # install deps (npm/python/gradle depending)
  ./run-minimal.sh --api-key $REDWOOD_KEY
  # observe streaming output in terminal

Debug heuristics (common friction hotspots)
- Auth failures: key missing or org mismatch. Check environment var and header.
- Streaming stalls: confirm HTTP/2 or chunked transfer is allowed by local proxy.
- Long tail latency: inspect 95p traces, check if client batching introduced queueing.
- Unexpected token counts: ensure prompt tokenizer matches the model tokenization; small differences between tokenizers cause billing confusion.

Minimal instrumentation template (one-liners)
- Log line format suggestion: {ts} {env} {request_id} model=model_name tokens_in=NN tokens_out=MM dur_ms=NNN status=200
- Save one sample trace to docs/trace-<date>.txt and attach to experiment notes.

Micro-experiment recipes (pick one per 48h):
- Recipe A: Warm-start comparison
  - Objective: measure cold vs warm KV cache impact
  - Steps: run 50 single short prompts (seq len ~50) with process restart between runs, then run 50 with continuous process; compare median latency.
- Recipe B: Quantization sanity check
  - Objective: confirm lightweight FFN quantized variant maintains output parity on small prompts
  - Steps: call model v1 (fp16) and v1-quant on same input set, diff tokens and semantic similarity (simple overlap).

Experiment notes template (one paragraph)
- Date:
- Author:
- Goal:
- Setup (sdk, model, flags):
- Steps run (commands):
- Key results (latency, cost delta, quality notes):
- Next action (rollback/expand/eng ticket):

Acceptance heuristics (when to escalate to eng/deeper support)
- Latency 95p > SLA target by >50% with small QPS (requests/sec < 5).
- Streaming appears truncated or missing tokens consistently.
- High quality regression vs baseline (nontrivial diffs across >30% of sample set).

Lab artifacts to capture (minimum)
- experiment/README.md (one-paragraph summary)
- experiment/raw-trace.log (1 representative trace)
- experiment/metrics.csv (timestamp, duration_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out)
- experiment/screenshots or terminal-recording.gif (if useful)

How to hand off a convincing POC to Solutions Eng
- Attach a single-file summary with: how to reproduce (commands), one failing/successful trace, and recommended next step (e.g., request dedicated capacity, configure prefix caching).

Open questions / TODOs (for this playbook)
- Shorten the Hello-path further for non-engineer product managers.
- Standardize a minimal JS + Python snippet that uses the same API verbatim.
- Add a tiny automated smoke-check action that runs the micro-experiment nightly for main examples.

References and links:
- SDK examples repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/examples
- Console quickstarts: console.redwood.ai/docs/quickstarts
- Tokenization note: confluence://DEVTOOLS/tokenization-quirks

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this file intentionally small — link to deeper guides.
- Share with Solutions Eng before next workshop.
- Capture one real customer anecdote and bake into the Hello-path (makes it stick).
